note:
Third attempt. Wave 2 produced the combination Malcolm asked for - a real elbow AND a gradual falloff - but the BOUND was still in the wrong place, and the reason is the crop window rather than the picture.

At a 1440 viewport a 4.42:1 master is shown from x0 = W - 1440/(440/H), which for 4096x928 is x=1058, i.e. the left 26% is never seen. Wave 2 said 'by 40 percent nothing of her remains', so its best candidate put the subject at 40% and left only 266px of heading ground, against 475px on the deterministic version already live. The other candidate placed a perfect elbow at 26% - exactly on the window edge - and measured 0px.

So the bound moves to 50 percent, which is where the live version's subject actually starts (1906 of 3750 = 51%) and what yields ~475px. The elbow moves with it, to 62-70 percent.

Do not zoom in, do not enlarge her, do not re-frame or crop closer. The remaining area to the LEFT continues the same scene. She is lying with her head resting on her own forearm; that forearm continues out of the supplied picture toward the left and the bend of her ELBOW is fully visible and complete, positioned between 62 and 70 percent of the frame width measured from the left edge. Beyond the elbow her upper arm recedes away from the key light and dissolves into deep shadow over a long, soft, entirely gradual falloff, with no hard edge, no abrupt cut and no visible boundary, so that by 50 percent of the frame width nothing of her remains.
